data.title: US Envoys Head To Kyiv After Talks With Putin On Ukraine War
data.description:
According to the BBC, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday after holding three hours of closed-door talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war in Ukraine. The White House said the pair discussed substantive next steps with Putin, while an announcement is expected in the coming weeks as efforts to end the conflict gather pace.

Putin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the meeting as constructive and extremely frank. He said the talks also covered economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects, and that the Russian side stressed the need to address the root causes of the conflict. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.

data.title: New Zealand National Party Pledges Easier Low-Deposit Mortgages for First-Time Buyers
data.description:

data.title: Virgin Atlantic Founder: Iran Conflict Is Unnecessary and Will Push Up Oil Prices
data.description: According to Jin10, Virgin Atlantic founder Richard Branson said in an interview in the United Kingdom on September 4 that the conflict with Iran is completely unnecessary and will only push up oil prices, raise costs for airlines and consumers, and bring inflation.

data.title: Middle East Oil Exports Fall Sharply After Iran War Shock, TankerTrackers Says
data.description: According to Jin10, TankerTrackers said Iraq's August oil exports fell 36% from pre-war levels after the outbreak of the U.S.-Israel war against Iran, making Iraq one of the Middle East producers with the largest export declines. Iran recorded the biggest drop, with crude exports plunging 100%, while Qatar and Saudi Arabia each saw exports fall 48%. Kuwait's August crude exports also declined 36%, matching Iraq and tying the two countries for third among the nations tracked by TankerTrackers, while the UAE saw the smallest decline at 0.02%.

data.title: Norway's Sovereign Wealth Fund Plans to Cut U.S. Treasury Holdings
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing CCTV Finance and CNBC, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, Norway's sovereign wealth fund, plans to adjust the share of government bonds in its portfolio, including reducing its U.S. Treasury holdings by about $80 billion to diversify risk exposure and improve returns.

The Norges Bank Investment Management unit that manages the fund wrote to Norway's Ministry of Finance on September 1, proposing to cut the weight of government bonds in the fund's benchmark bond index from 70% to 50%; the letter was made public on the 4th. The fund currently has less than 26% of its total assets in fixed-income assets. Under the proposed adjustment, its allocation to U.S. Treasuries would fall by 12.2 percentage points to 21.9%, which is estimated to reduce holdings by about $80 billion. The proposal still needs review by the Ministry of Finance and parliament, and a final decision is expected in spring 2027.

CNBC said the move comes at a sensitive time for the U.S. Treasury market, as investors worry about the U.S. fiscal outlook and a growing debt burden, while long-dated yields have climbed to a 10-year high. Economists said the planned reduction is not large, but it sends an important signal that the willingness of traditional government bond holders and buyers to absorb supply is declining.

The fund manages about $2.34 trillion in assets and invests in about 7,100 companies across more than 50 countries and regions. Data showed that its investment return in the first half of this year reached 1.75 trillion Norwegian kroner, a record high.

data.title: Former BOC Securities Fund Manager Sues Employer Over Labor Contract Dispute
data.description:
Jiemian News reported that Shanghai High People's Court has disclosed a hearing notice showing that former BOC Securities fund manager Ji Wei has sued his former employer over a labor contract dispute. The case is scheduled to be heard on October 19, 2026, at the Pudong New Area People's Court in Shanghai.

Ji joined BOC Securities in October 2019 and was once head of its ETF investment team. He left all funds under management on September 5, 2025, citing resignation. The article said his ETF products delivered mixed results, while several actively managed products posted losses, including BOC Securities Ruiyi Flexible Allocation Mixed A, which returned -38.18% during his tenure. Before joining BOC Securities, Ji had worked at Huaan Fund and Huian Fund, where he previously managed Huian Fengze A with a 52.14% tenure return.

The article also said BOC Securities reported stronger first-half 2026 results, with revenue up 27.7% year on year to 1.922 billion yuan and net profit attributable to shareholders up 32.05% to 746 million yuan. Its total assets rose 37.08% to 127.377 billion yuan. However, the firm’s public fund business remained heavily tilted toward fixed income: as of the second quarter of 2026, stock and mixed funds together accounted for only 3.12% of total assets under management, while bond funds and money market funds dominated the portfolio.

data.title: Iraq's August Oil Exports Fall 36% From Pre-Conflict Levels, TankerTrackers Says
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, maritime shipping tracker TankerTrackers said on Saturday that Iraq's August oil exports fell 36% from levels before the U.S.-Iran conflict began. The comparison used January-February export data as the pre-conflict baseline.

Iran posted the largest decline, with oil exports down 100%. Qatar and Saudi Arabia followed, with exports in both countries down 48%. Kuwait's August oil exports also fell 36%, matching Iraq and tying for third among the countries tracked by TankerTrackers. The United Arab Emirates saw the smallest drop, with oil exports down just 0.02% from pre-war levels.

data.title: Cathie Wood Says Strong Jobs Report Signals New Economy Formation
data.description:
ARK Invest founder Cathie Wood said Friday’s jobs report was strong, with nonfarm payrolls rising by 162,000 and household survey employment increasing by more than 500,000. According to ChainCatcher, she said the average workweek also increased and that the economy was operating well in August.

Wood said many people will see more inflation and Federal Reserve tightening, but she sees a larger shift underway. She pointed to overall inflation at 3.7%, while other measures are closer to 2%.

She also said oil prices could fall toward $30, stocks are hitting record highs as interest rates rise, capital spending has broken above a more than 20-year ceiling, Bitcoin is moving away from gold, and companies embracing artificial intelligence are creating jobs faster.

Wood said these are not isolated signals and may mark the start of stronger real growth and powerful technology-driven disinflation. She added that consensus is pricing in the old economy, while she believes a new economy is forming.

data.title: Arbitrum Founder and Solana Co-Founder Debate Robinhood Chain Fee Model
data.description:
Arbitrum founder Steven Goldfeder and Solana co-founder Toly debated Robinhood Chain's fee model on September 6. According to PANews, Toly said Robinhood Chain's 10% revenue share to Arbitrum would be enough to cover four times Solana's on-chain transaction fees, suggesting user gas fees could be lower if the chain were deployed on Solana.

Goldfeder said Robinhood could keep about 90% of gas revenue under Arbitrum's architecture, and that the choice of Arbitrum was made to "be the landlord, not the tenant." Toly replied that Robinhood could charge fees at the application front end while using a lower-cost base network. Goldfeder said much of the on-chain activity does not pass through Robinhood's front end, and that if Robinhood were only a tenant on the base network, it would not earn revenue from those peripheral activities.

Market reports said Robinhood evaluated Solana and Arbitrum during the product planning stage and ultimately chose Arbitrum, which can deploy its own chain independently.

data.title: Putin Says Russia Has Halted Airstrikes on Kyiv From Midnight
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Russian President Vladimir Putin met with U.S. President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner at the Kremlin on the evening of the 5th, discussed details of a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, and said Russia would work to ensure the safety of the U.S.-Ukraine talks process and mediators. Putin said Russia had received requests through its intelligence and diplomatic channels to stop airstrikes on Kyiv and that he had issued the relevant order, with airstrikes on Kyiv halted from midnight.

data.title: South Korean Banks' Corporate Dollar Deposits Hit Record High This Month
data.description:
Data released on Sunday showed that corporate dollar deposits at major South Korean banks hit a record high this month as the won fell to a near two-year low against the U.S. dollar. According to Sina Finance, the dollar deposit balance at South Korea's five largest domestic banks reached $76.98 billion as of Thursday, the highest level since the statistic was first compiled in May 2021.

The five banks are KB Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Hana Bank, Woori Bank, and NH Nonghyup Bank. At 10:30 p.m. on Friday, the won was quoted at 1,345 per dollar, its strongest level since October 8, 2024, when the rate was 1,344.6 per dollar.

Compared with the record low of 1,588.2 per dollar set on July 1, the won had recovered 254.2 won. Shinhan Bank economist Baek Seok-hyun said exporters were delaying the conversion of foreign-exchange earnings into won, which pushed up dollar deposits, while importers were also buying dollars in stages.

Demand to exchange won into dollars has also been rising. Data showed that in the first three days of this month, the five banks' total won-to-dollar exchange volume reached $60 million. Monthly exchange volume was $275 million in February, fell sharply to $164 million in June, and rebounded to $349 million in July.

An NH Nonghyup Bank official said individuals began buying dollars as the won weakened in July and August, and demand for dollars to invest in U.S. stocks also increased.
